newsitem.title: ROMANIA: E.European stocks gain ground before holiday.
newsitem.headline: E.European stocks gain ground before holiday.

text.p: Most East European stock markets staged a good show in the shorter week ahead of May Day holidays, with Budapest outshining the others with two consecutive highs.
A bull run in Bucharest hoisted high-caps and most second- tier stocks and Slovenian and Croatian shares also picked up.
Polish shares fell slightly on the week but made a recovery on Wednesday and in Prague shares eased as a government package failed to rekindle investor interest.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which measures price movements in 73 Hungarian, Polish, Czech, Slovak and Slovenian stocks, slipped marginally.
With the exception of Prague, all East European markets are closed on Thursday and Friday.
BUDAPEST
The Dow's rally and earnings reports drove Hungarian shares higher, leading the BUX index to two successive record highs.
The bourse also registered its highest daily turnover of 9.177 billion forints on Wednesday, when the BUX closed at a record high of 5,985.17 points, more than three percent up from last Friday.

"The Budapest bourse will be closed on Thursday and Friday, while London will be closed on Monday, therefore many investors might have brought forward their purchases," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities. "Of course, the Dow's rally contributed, too."
One of the week's strong gainers was Richter, which soared after its first quarter results had been released, while chemicals TVK gained on expectations of strong January-March earnings.
PRAGUE
Czech shares continued to lose ground over the course of the week, as the government's recent package of measures designed to stimulate growth failed to revive investor optimism.
The Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 index eased 8.9 points, or 1.65 percent, on the week to a 1997 low of 538.8, pulled lower by blue chip losses.

The government announced on April 16 a series of sweeping measures aimed at reviving the economy and capital markets, but analysts said the moves had failed to lure back investors who have shunned Czech shares due to poor market transparency.
Many shares -- including SPT Telecom and Komercni Banka -- also lost ground after posting lower than expected first quarter results.
WARSAW

Polish shares fell 0.7 percent this week to 16,546.7 points but gained on Wednesday after Tuesday's Dow surge, and analysts said eyes might remain on Wall Street in the next two days when Polish markets are closed for holidays.
"On Thursday and Friday important macroeconomic information will be released in the U.S. so there's a chance there'll be swings from that," said Pawel Hominski, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.
U.S. employment data are due on Friday.

Analysts said a negative sign was the Polish central bank's decision last Friday to increase mandatory reserves on zloty term deposits from April 30, with banks especially vulnerable. Most banks fell this week.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks forged ahead this week and traders said strong demand would keep prices high.

Blue chip Drugs firm Pliva led gainers, ending on 490 on Thursday, up 24 kuna from last Friday. Another fully-listed issue, Zagrebacka Banka, recovered to 2,183 kuna, still down from last Friday's 2,200.
Both blue chips also rose in London but traders put down investor interest in the stocks to collecting the dividend, which both companies are due to pay out in June.
Another gainer was textile firm Varteks, which ended on 85 kuna, up from last week's 74, following the news the U.S. giant Levi Strauss & Co had extended its licence for five more years.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares firmed 0.11 percent this week, with the blue-chip SBI index rising by 1.46 points to 1,316.56. Turnover fell to 140.7 million tolars from 176.6 million.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank were the top gainers, jumping 5.36 percent, while brokerage Finmedia led decliners, falling 7.1 percent.

Traders said stagnation on the market would continue until foreign capital returned to the market as domestic investors did not have enough money to support a constant growth of the market, which expects new listings next month.
BUCHAREST
The Bucharest stock exchange's four first-tier listings held centre-stage this week amid bullish sentiment gripping high-caps since last week.
Heavy trading and higher prices sent two independent indices to year highs for the sixth consecutive session.
Three of the four heavyweights climbed on Wednesday, with Azomures fertiliser maker racing ahead with a 43 percent rise in its average price to 3,676 lei. It closed higher at 3,800.
Second-tier trading was subdued.
